column1: # The UI refresh's coverage table (docs/specs/ui-refresh-plan.md section 2.1): every file in OpenPmsDental/UI, CodeBase/UI (UI-PLAIN),
# WpfControlsOD/UI and WpfControlsOD/Themes has a row here with the package that restyles it, or the reason it keeps its look. NoHqTests' UiCoverageTests fails when a
# file has no row, when a file matches more than one row, or when a row matches no file, so a new control or a new shared dictionary cannot slip
# through. Package UI-1 wrote its first version from section 2.1.
# files: the file's path relative to the repository root, with forward slashes and without its extensions (a designer, .resx, .xaml and .xaml.cs
# file goes with its main file: Button.cs, Button.designer.cs and Button.resx are OpenPmsDental/UI/Button); * matches any characters.
# package: the packages that restyle it, comma-separated (UI-1 to UI-11 of section 7), or keeps (it keeps its look, the note says why), or
# no-drawing (it draws nothing of its own; windows among them get the frame and controls like any window). note: what, in a few words.

column3: the combo box's frame over the stock single-line inputs (text box, up-down box, date picker) and, polish round, every multi-line text box; fix round, every bordered rich text box (ODtextBox), single-line ones too; UI-13: the corners in the parent's colour on whole pixels, and the other shared looks attached with it (AttachOne); fix round 2: the themed date picker's whole drop button covered (DTM_GETDATETIMEPICKERINFO), its value in the Text token, a disabled picker's box in the disabled grey; UI-PLAIN: moved to CodeBase, attached to the plain windows by UiPlainWindow

the stock date picker's drop-down calendar: the program's MonthCalendarOD instead of Windows' calendar pop-up (its drop button, F4 and Alt+Down), the picker's events as Windows raises them; UI-CAL-2: wholly on the picker's screen (GetDropBounds)
the stock radio button drawn like the program's check box (round 3: the circle where the box is, the text 16 px from the left); UI-13: a circle on the right drawn there in the same look
the stock up-down box's arrow buttons drawn like the combo box's drop area (polish round: the box's fill, the Fluent chevrons)

every scroll bar (the stock scroll bar controls of the grids, lists and pickers, and the frame scroll bars of text boxes, lists, tree and list views, scrolling panels) painted over in UiScrollPaint's Fluent look
